old: An induction gathers scattered attention until quieter material becomes easier to hear. You don’t have to surrender, play asleep, or obey anyone. When you’re sober, distracted, analytical, or guarded, an actual induction may help. When meditation, loveyhuasca, lucid dreaming, grief, music, prayer, fatigue, or another intense opening has already made you trancey, begin with orientation and containment instead of adding depth.
new: Note: Using an induction will help your focus, making it easier to tap into the more esoteric parts of this work. That said, you don’t need to go into a trance state, play asleep, or give up your power to anyone. If you’re sober and distracted, or too analytical or guarded to easily reach the parts of you that need this work, it may be helpful to use an actual induction. However, if you’ve already gone into a trancey state through meditation or loveyhuasca or lucid dreaming, or you are freshly grieving or have been deeply moved by music or prayer or you are simply sleep deprived, you may want to skip ahead to the orientation and containment sections.

old: Aim for the amount of trance that suits the practice: focused, warm, receptive, embodied, and still able to stop. Depth is optional.
new: A note on how deep of a trance you need to go into for this work:

old: Prepare the session, gather attention, deepen only when that helps, then let what you notice shape the words and the next response. Counting is one way in. Conversation, story, movement, repeated sound, and curiosity can also organize attention. Say so when you use them; elegance doesn’t excuse a covert induction.
new: There is a real benefit to preparing a session before you start and once you've gathered your subject's attention you can deepen if necessary but you're free to start wording up if the context of the session requires it. You can use a number of ways to organise your subject's attention, counting is but one and if you're going to use it then say so. You can use conversation, stories, movement, repeated sounds, or simply curiosity etc... But if you're going to use them say so. Elegence is always useful, but not at the expense of doing something that you shouldn't be doing.

old: For a simple, chosen target, you can test the suggestion before deepening. If the useful response is already happening, build from it. An induction helps you find a receptive way of listening; you don’t need to complete a ceremony before you’re allowed to respond.
new: Also, with a simple enough target, why not try it first and if it works then deepen.

old: Choose one purpose, one starting anchor or image, and a way back. Decide whether warmth, a firm boundary, direction, or neutral witnessing would help. Floating, stairs, gardens, inner rooms, colored light, and child dialogue do not all need to report for duty at once. Switch consciously when the metaphor stops helping.
new: Client is king so you need to pick one purpose for the induction, one starting place, anchor or image, and one way to get back. Then you can bring in any of the other ingredients you want, but in a conscious way. If you feel the need to switch metaphors, do so consciously. You may want to bring in some feelings of warmth, or of setting boundaries, or of direction, or of being a neutral witness. You may want to use floating, stairs, gardens, going to an inner room, colored lights, talking to your inner child. It doesn't all have to be used.

old: Imagery is optional. A signal may arrive through sensation, rhythm, movement, words, spatial sense, simple knowing, or no response at all. Keep the language in the world you chose: let a count mark something meaningful there, and reverse the journey when you finish. Borrow qualities such as warmth or steadiness without replacing your identity.
new: You don't even need to use imagery. You can use any sense, rhythm, body movement, words, spatial sense, intuitive knowledge, or even no response at all to create the signal. Just be sure to use your chosen world when counting and when coming out of the induction. You can borrow qualities from other worlds, just be sure you don't borrow them into your own identity.

old: Pick one central verb, one sensory quality, one short refrain, and one transition phrase, then read the script aloud; long elegant sentences become soup during an induction.
new: Start simple. Choose one verb, one sensory quality, one short refrain, and one way of transitioning. Read your script out loud - it's easy to get carried away writing long, elegant sentences that turn into soup when you start the induction.

old: Bring your chosen concern lightly to mind, or remain with your wish for contact. Let it be present without rehearsing its whole story.
new: Bring to mind, lightly, what it is that you want to contact. Or simply, stay with the wish to contact.

old: What am I noticing now?
new: What do you notice now?

old: Give the response time to take its own form. It might be a sensation, a few words, an image, a feeling, or an impulse to move. There may be nothing clear yet.
new: Allow yourself some time to notice what is coming. It might be sensations, words, images, feelings, the urge to move in some way or nothing at all.

old: Leave room to notice, with words or without them.
new: Allow yourself some time to notice this, with or without words.

old: Use this when loveyhuasca, meditation, lucid dreaming, grief, music, prayer, erotic energy, exhaustion, or intense beauty has already opened the state. Stabilize before making it stronger.
“The state is already open. I do not need to intensify it. I need to aim it, stabilize it, and keep it kind.”

Look around the room. Name where you are. Name the date, or at least the day. Feel your feet, hands, and spine. Press your thumbs gently but firmly against your index fingers. Focus on the physical friction of skin meeting skin.
“Only what can be integrated is welcome now. Anything too much can wait. The body may stay safe. The adult self remains present. The inner child does not have to carry this alone.”
Once you’re oriented, choose one intention:
“Please show me the next useful truth, symbol, feeling, question, or action — only in the amount I can live well with.”
new: This is most useful after you have already opened yourself to a state, through loveyhuasca, meditation, lucid dreaming, dealing with grief, listening to music, prayer, engagement with erotic energy, exhaustion, or being overwhelmed by beauty. This is to stabilize your state, not to make it stronger.
I already have an open state, now I want to aim that open state and make it stronger.
Look around you, orient yourself to where you are, what date it is. Focus on the physical sensation of squeezing your thumbs against your index fingers, feel the friction.
Now, I will only allow myself to go as far as I can integrate. My body will be safe, my adult self is here, my inner child doesn't have to do this alone.
Now, tell me the next thing I need to know, in symbols, feelings, questions, actions, in doses that I can integrate.

old: Sit upright. Open the eyes. Feel the feet. Let the breath be natural.
new: You can do this practice sitting up, with your eyes open, etc.

old: Say: “I am not going away. I am coming more fully here.”
new: Begin by saying to yourself that you are not going to go away in this practice, you are coming more.

old: Look at one object. Feel the spine.
new: Then choose an object to look at, or feel your spine, etc.

old: “Is this daydream guidance, emotional digestion, or avoidance?”
new: Ask yourself if your daydreaming is helping you to receive guidance or digest emotional experiences, or if you are escaping from something.

old: “If it is guidance, show me the action inside it. If it is avoidance, bring me gently into the present and show me what I am avoiding.”
new: Then you can ask for help to take action based on the guidance or to come into the present moment and see what you are escaping from.

old: If stillness makes you sleepy, diffuse, or escape-prone, hypnosis can become more alert rather than more relaxed. Keep the eyes open and pair a small repeated hand movement with increasing clarity; stop the movement and notice what remains without trying to disappear inward.
new: If you find that being still leads you to escape into sleepiness and diffuse states, you can work with increasing alertness rather than relaxation, keep your eyes open and work with doing a movement with your hands, which you repeat for a while and then stop deliberately in order to notice if there is any residual activity.

old: “Eyes open. Press thumb and forefinger together gently. Release. Again — clearer, not sleepier. One more time. Now stop the deliberate movement. Notice the first second after the rhythm ends. Is there an echo in the fingers, the breath, the attention, or nowhere at all? Stay upright and work from exactly that level of alertness.”
new: You can say something like: ‘While you keep your eyes open, press your thumb and forefinger together and then let go; do this a few times, becoming more and more clear and alert each time. Now deliberately stop doing that movement and notice if there is any residual activity or if it has completely stopped.’ Work with a level of alertness that is useful to you.

old: Place one hand on the heart. Place the other hand on the solar plexus.
new: Where are YOUR hands? Put one on YOUR heart and the other on YOUR solar plexis.

old: Let the heart hand represent the Nurturer. Let the solar plexus hand represent the vulnerable child.
new: The hand on YOUR heart is the Nurturer, the one on the solar plexis is the little vulnerable part in YOU.

old: Breathe gently.
new: Then breath and affirm

old: “Love above. Child below. Adult present.”
new: “ The love is above and the child is below. And in the middle, the adult – that’s ME!

old: “I send love to the child. I receive the child’s signal. I send love again. I listen again.”
new: I send love down and I receive the signal from the child. Then I send love again and receive the signal again.

old: Fractionation means returning toward ordinary awareness and then deciding whether to enter absorption again. Used openly, it teaches that trance has a door in both directions. Name the technique before using it; every answer cannot secretly mean “deeper.”
new: Fractionation is a term for going out and back into a deeper stage of absorption. If you use it openly you need to make it clear that you are using it as that will help you avoid the problem of all answers leading to going deeper.

old: “Open the eyes and return toward ordinary awareness. Feel the room and decide whether to stop here. If you choose to continue, close or soften the eyes and notice what changes as attention gathers again. You may stop at either point.”
new: Open your eyes and come back out to normal awareness. You can choose to stop at this point if you want to. If you want to go deeper then simply close or soften your eyes again and notice the difference. Of course you can stop at this point if you want to.

old: “If it is useful, attention may become more gathered. If it is not useful, I remain exactly as awake as I need to be.”
new: Remind yourself, 'If this is useful to me in this moment, my attention will become gathered. If this is not useful, I will still be as awake as I need to be.'

old: Choose one simple scene: a room in the heart, a garden, a temple, a fire with the Protector nearby, a clear lake, or a chair where the adult waits. One scene is plenty.
new: Imagine a scene that would help keep up the attention on what is useful to attend to. It could be that of being in a place within the heart, a garden, a temple, near a fire with the Protector nearby, at a lake, or simply being with the adult sitting in a comfortable chair. Create one scene that will be sufficient.

old: “Who or what needs to speak first?”
new: “Who or what needs to speak first?”

old: “As I wait, I give up the responsibility of making anything happen.
new: And then I simply wait. I give over the responsibility.

old: If it is useful, the wise subconscious may let one finger twitch, pulse, lift, warm, tingle, or become subtly noticeable when the inner meeting space is ready.
new: If it is useful at this time, my wise subconscious will allow some signal to come through – one finger will begin to twitch, or pulse, or lift, or warm, or tingle, or become noticeable to me in some way, showing that there is now a place for me to meet with it.

old: I will not force it. I will not fake it. I will simply wait with love and notice.”
new: I don’t force this, I don’t fake this, I just wait with love and notice.

old: A finger may move, a hand may warm, the breath may change, or nothing may happen. None proves truth; at most, something may be listening.
new: It may or it may not. But neither proves the truth of it – it may still be listening.

old: Pacing and leading means stating what is already true before inviting anything new.
new: What is Pacing and Leading?

old: “Anxiety is here. The body is activated. A protector is trying to help. And one breath at a time, the adult can start to listen.”
new: “Even though the anxiety is here, and the activation in the body is here, and even though that protector is doing its’ best, one breath at a time the adult in me is here to listen.”

old: The simplest form is a Truth + Invite loop:
new: Pacing and Leading is as simple as:

old: “It is completely true that [current sensation or emotion] is here. It makes sense that my system is reacting by [current protective behavior or thought]. And right alongside that truth, my adult self is here, breathing in this room, ready to listen to whatever comes up next.”
new: “It is completely true that (insert current sensation or emotion), and it is completely true that (insert current behavior or thought as a protective response), and at the same time the adult in me is here, breathing in this room, and ready to listen.”

old: Awareness verbs point attention without yelling at it: notice, realize, recognize, sense, feel, wonder, imagine, picture, listen, allow, discover, remember, consider.
new: What’s the purpose of Awareness Verbs? To help with awareness, obviously! But how? The easiest way to explain is probably through an example. So, let’s say that after a question, instead of saying ‘Take a moment to think about it’, instead, using one of the Awareness Verbs from the list at the bottom, perhaps it could be ‘Take a moment to notice the answer’. Or even, ‘notice what form the answer takes’. What difference does it make?

old: “Notice whether the answer comes as an image, a word, a pressure, a warmth, a silence, or a next action.”
new: Here is a list of Awareness verbs: Notice Realize Recognise Sense Feel Wonder Imagine Picture Listen Allow Discover Remember Consider

old: Words such as as, while, because, when, after, before, and which means connect one event to another. Use them carefully. A gentle voice doesn’t make a false causal claim true.
new: It’s important to be very careful when using the words, “as, while, because, when, after, before,” or “which means.”

old: Too strong: “Because I breathe, the trauma leaves.” Better: “As I breathe, the adult self may become present enough to hear one small piece of what the wound needs.”
new: Why? Well, because these words are saying that one thing is causing the other, and that’s usually too strong a statement to be true!

old: An embedded invitation places a small direction inside a larger sentence. It should invite a modest inner movement, not hide a demand.
new: Embedded Invitations are invitations embedded in a larger sentence.

old: “And somewhere inside this breath, I can let the adult self listen.”
new: Example of an embedded invitation:

old: “As I sit here, I may allow one small truth to become clear.”
new: Another example of an embedded invitation:

old: “The child does not have to trust me all at once; it can simply notice I am still here.”
new: Yet another example of an embedded invitation:

old: Use one when it helps. Ten embedded invitations in a row feel like somebody took a weekend certification.
new: The question is not whether to use embedded invitations, but how many. Ten embedded invitations in a row makes people think that “this person must have just gotten certified.”

old: The Milton Model opens possibility. The Meta Model asks exactly what somebody means. Ethical practice needs both.
new: To ‘Milton Model’ is to open things up. To ‘Meta Model’ is to ask “What do yo mean by that?” In order to be truly effective (and ethical) with people, it is necessary to do both.

old: “How specifically?” “According to whom?” “Compared to what?” “Always?” “Never?” “What exactly would happen?” “How do I know?” “What evidence would change my mind?”
new: “What do yo mean ‘Specifically’? According to who? ‘Good’ compared to what? ‘Always’? ‘Never’? What specifically would happen? How do yo know? What would constitute proof for ya?”

old: Use Milton Model to soften into the body. Use Meta Model to return to truth.
new: If, in session, it feels like the body is stiffening up, ‘Milton’ it. If it feels like truth is eluding ya, ‘Meta’ it.

old: Fear, craving, fantasy, belief, and memory may have sensory qualities: near or far, bright or dim, loud or quiet, moving or still, heavy or light, inside or outside the body. Work with qualities you actually notice. If none are apparent, skip this tool rather than inventing an image or voice.
new: Pattern Disruption tool: Properties If your fear, craving, fantasy, belief or memory has any sensory properties (it looks or sounds near or far, bright or dim, loud or quiet, or it moves, is heavy, is inside or outside your body etc) then you can work with its properties. If it doesn't have any properties then don't try to force it, just skip this tool.

old: Ask how the experience is represented. What changes when the image moves two feet back, the voice gets quieter, or the edge becomes less sharp?
new: Ask yourself: How is your

old: “I am not deleting the signal. I am adjusting the volume so I can listen without being overwhelmed.”
new: "I'm not deleting the signal, I'm just adjusting the volume."

old: Before moving one imaginary pixel, ask the guard whether that change is acceptable.
new: Before changing a pixel, ask the guard for permission:

old: “Would it be okay if we moved this image back just a little, or lowered the volume slightly, purely so my adult self can stay present enough to hear what you need to tell me?”
new: "Would it be OK if I moved the image a bit further away or turned the volume down a little bit? This will allow me to hear you better with my adult brain.

old: I’m speaking from experience in this appendix.
new: I’m writing this appendix from a place of experience.

old: During self-hypnosis, meditation, lucid dreaming, loveyhuasca, grief, prayer, plant-medicine-adjacent practice, or other altered states, people sometimes meet something that doesn’t feel like an ordinary emotion or younger part. It may appear as a demon, jinn, parasitic energy, dark intelligence, or terrifying archetype—a voice or image that feels intrusive, hateful, seductive, mocking, or simply alien.
new: Sometimes, in self-hypnosis, meditation, lucid dreaming, loveyhuasca, periods of grief, prayer, or other altered states of consciousness, people encounter something that isn’t just an emotion, or a young part. It may seem like a demon, jinn, parasitic energy, dark intelligence, terrifying archetypal being, or come as a voice or image of some sort. Whatever it is, it’s unwanted, intrusive, and seemingly full of hate, or seduction, or mockery, or just feels different.

old: I don’t need this guide to settle the metaphysics. Perhaps these are literal beings. Perhaps they are symbolic mind-forms, trauma in a frightening costume, dissociated energy, or ancestral and relational burdens. The practical question is:
new: Do I need to provide a guide for what these beings might be? Maybe they are literal beings. Maybe they are a symbolic form the mind creates to hold difficult feelings, past trauma, dissociated energy, or things picked up from parents, partners, or ancestors. It doesn’t matter. The question is:

old: “What response makes me safer, clearer, more loving, more grounded, and less hooked?”
new: What is the best way to respond to them, in order to feel safe, clear, loving, grounded, and un-hooked?

old: When a demonic, jinn-like, hostile, or intrusive presence appears, don’t reward it with instant metaphysical certainty. Run the triage first: medical danger, environment, body, overload, and how open the mind has become. Open the eyes, feel the feet, name the room, lower stimulation, leave hostile company, and stop adding prompts. Don’t deepen, hunt for hidden truth, or debate ontology while destabilized.
new: Do this when seeing/encountering a demonic/jinn-like or other hostile or intrusive presence: This is a quick reference to the basics of the triage steps, medical danger, environment, body, overload, and mind opened. Open eyes, make sure of environmental safety, feel connection with body such as feet on floor, reduce environmental stimulation, remove yourself from any hostile environments or people, stop doing anything that would increase stimulation to the mind. Do not attempt to go deeper, to find out more, to be ontological, or do anything to increase destabilization.

old: “Only what can be integrated is welcome now. Anything too much can wait. The adult self remains present. The body may return to safety.”
new: Mantra: Only what can be integrated is allowed at this time. If it is too much, it can wait. The adult self is always available to be there. Return the body to a safe place.

old: Danger to self or others, psychosis-like fear, inability to sleep, extreme paranoia, chest pain, seizures, serious overheating, overdose concern, or loss of basic functioning means the self-hypnosis session is over. Get real-world help.
new: If at any time during self-hypnosis sessions, if there is danger to yourself or others, if things become too scary and psychosis-like, if unable to sleep, if feeling extremely paranoid, if experiencing chest pain, seizures, serious overheating, drug or other substance overdose, or inability to function, the session is over, and help should be sought in the real world.

old: Once you’re stable enough to stay present, notice what helps without turning the response into a metaphysical test. Put a hand on the heart if that feels welcome, take a comfortable breath, and keep the room available.
new: 1. Come into a stable state, if needed put your hand on your heart, etc.

old: I don’t have to decide what this is right now. I can notice whether warmth or distance helps, and keep my boundary either way. Nothing here requires my obedience.
new: 2. Internalize that you do not have to know what this is. Ask yourself if it would be appropriate to send it some warmth or if you need to place a boundary with it. Know that you are under no obligation to do whatever it is asking of you.

old: If vulnerability appears—a knot in the throat, sadness, fear, or a sense of trying to protect something—you can bring in the Nurturer. If the experience remains hostile or becomes more frightening, stop engaging with it and return to the body and room.
new: 3. If you feel vulnerable, tightness in your throat, sadness, fear or you sense you need to protect yourself in some manner, bring in your Nurturer. If it continues to be hostile or you feel afraid, then do not continue to engage with it.

old: Neither response establishes its origin. A protective part needn’t reveal its fear quickly; a comforting response doesn’t prove an interpretation either. The useful question is whether this way of responding helps you become clearer, steadier, and less hooked. Love and boundaries don’t require a verdict first.
new: 4. Again, you do not have to know where this is coming from. Ask yourself if this way of responding to it seems to be clearing it. It is ok to use a combination of love and boundaries to interact with it.

old: The first impulse may be to fight, banish, hate, prove power, argue, panic, or identify completely with the threatened self. Some traditions use prayers, mantras, protections, banishing rituals, or exorcism forms, and some people find them useful. But fighting from fear can fasten attention more tightly to the thing you want gone.
new: My first thought is to fight it, banish it, hate it, show it I’m more powerful, argue with it, panic, be it, etc. I have seen different prayers, mantras, protections, banishing and exorcism forms that some people find useful. The problem is, if you fight from fear…

old: Fear gives it center stage. Hatred gives it a hook. Pride gives it an opponent. Panic gives it the nervous system.
new: …it becomes the center of your attention and when you hate it, give it a hook in you, or fight it from pride or panic….

old: “I do not need to hate this. I do not need to merge with this. I do not need to obey this. I do not need to defeat this from fear. I return to loving awareness.”
new: “I do not need to hate you. I do not need to become you. I do not need to listen to you. I do not need to fight you from fear. I simply return my attention to loving awareness.”

old: When the presence feels hostile, cold, alien, parasitic, or boundary-violating, don’t offer soft sentimental love as though inviting it in for tea. Use love with a boundary.
new: Often when I sense a presence I feel it to be not so good, a little hostile, cold, alien, parasitic, violating. To project soft sentimental mush to it is like inviting it in for tea. Instead use something like this:

old: Sit upright. Press your feet into the floor. Let the spine rise. Gently draw the shoulder blades back so the chest is open but not exposed. Feel the skin boundary of the torso. Feel that this body has a perimeter.
new: Sit up, bring your feet down, lift up with your spine, bring your shoulders back gently, feel the skin boundary of your torso, feel the perimeter of your body, and say:

old: “I recognize that suffering may be here, and I wish all suffering to return to the space where it belongs. But the boundary of this skin belongs to my adult life. You do not have permission to enter this house.”
new: Even if I sense there is suffering here, which is to be wished well, I am returning all of that to its own space. The skin boundary is where my adult life exists. You may not come into this house.

old: “Compassion is present. The door is closed.”
new: “Compassion is present. The door is closed.”

old: Preview the sequence, choose one purpose, and decide whether you want to begin. Each family can be light, eyes-open, or replaced by no-trance contact. Notice the actual response—including no change—and let it determine the next move. Move, imagine, change the sensory channel, remain still, or stop. Use the complete waking return after every induction.
new: To use any of these sequences you first read over them, decide if you want to use them and if you do you start working with them. You adapt them to suit the family by using lighter versions, keeping the eyes open or using no trance contact instead of induction if appropriate. Then you see what happens including nothing happening and from that you decide what to do next. Maybe move on to the next part of the sequence, or imagine what you are describing, or use a different sensory channel, or just sit there in silence or maybe stop completely. At the end of each induction you bring the family back up to full waking consciousness.

old: If vivid images don’t come, translate the metaphor into words, rhythm, spatial sense, touch, movement, or simple knowing. The mind doesn’t owe anybody a movie.
new: If the family are having difficulty imagining anything vividly you can translate the metaphors into a different sensory channel or just talk about them, give the rhythm, describe the space, touch the family, move them or just know what you mean.

old: Feel the support beneath you and the position of one hand or foot. Press gently, stretch slightly, and release—or imagine it. Notice ease, tension, warmth, breath, or no change. Repeat with no more than three areas, letting “release” guide the sequence. Which area or inner voice wants attention? What support is needed? Restore ordinary movement and return.
new: Starting Point: Lie on the floor and/or place yourself in a position where you can feel support under one hand or foot. Gently press and/or stretch and then release the area. Note any sensations, or just imagine the press/stretch/release. Repeat with a maximum of three areas. Use the word ‘release’ to guide you. Now move or not – whichever feels most alive. See if you can sense what’s emerging; an area, a voice within. Try to find a way of supporting what wants your attention. When ready, restore movement and return.

old: Notice where your weight is carried. Let support carry 1% more effort, as if floating without losing contact, or keep ordinary weight and pressure. Notice the response. You may deliberately alternate attention toward ordinary awareness on the inhale and support on the exhale; name this fractionation beforehand. What becomes easier to hear? Keep the support, regain chosen weight and firm contact, then return.
new: Try for a moment to let yourself feel that you are not weighting down upon your support at all, then try feeling as though you were weighting just a tiny bit- only one percent- of the effort onto the support, so that you are almost floating above it. Then try feeling your normal amount of weighting down and pressure upon it. Notice if there are any differences that you feel. (You can try to fractionate this by switching your attention back and forth between the normal weighting and the supported weighting, perhaps on in breaths and out breaths. If you are going to do that, be aware that you are doing it before you begin.) Then you can return back to normal weighting, firmly touching your support, as you choose.

old: Accompany a natural rhythm: breath, a comfortable hum, a finger tap, outside sound, or silent counting. No rhythm is also an option. Repeat “here, and here again,” noticing where attention lands between repetitions. Stop the deliberate rhythm and notice the first quiet beat, without trying to become blank. Is a word, feeling, need, or action clearer? Let ordinary rhythm resume and return.
new: Try it with a natural rhythm; perhaps the rhythm of breathing or a slight hum in the throat. Try it with a more artificial rhythm, such as tapping a finger or listening to sounds outside. Even try it counting (silently) to yourself, or even with no rhythm at all. Say the words 'here, and here again' over and over, until suddenly, stop the rhythm. This will bring about its own rhythm, the first one that appears - do not try and make it blank. This might bring a bit more clarity to what word, feeling, need or action is coming up. Then go back to using a normal rhythm.

old: Notice a concern with several strands. Imagine yarn unwinding, bubbles settling, or knots placed visibly beside you. Leave the object unchanged or label it in words when that fits better. Count only strands you actually set down; nothing is erased. Which needs warmth, protection, or action? Keep one useful strand, give the others a visible holding place, and return.
new: A quick exercise for when you have several concerns going on. Visualise each one as a strand of yarn, or even better, have some by you to help. When you've placed them all, take a minute to look at them all (without changing them, though you could label them if needed, by saying a word or two). How many did you end up with? Now pick one that is important to do something about, put the others somewhere you can see them, and come back to this page.

old: Hear the actual room and feel the body before imagining a step toward a chosen destination. Use footsteps, textures, or landmarks to gather attention. Change scenery or skip directly to dialogue when useful. Notice a detail without assigning hidden meaning; the mystery is how the scene develops, not what will be done to you. Who or what needs to speak? Return by the same route and close the imagined space.
new: Ground yourself in your current physical space by noticing the acoustics of the room and sensing your body. Visualize stepping purposefully toward your chosen location. As you "walk," focus your attention by gathering information about the surroundings through auditory and tactile senses, such as listening to your footsteps, feeling textures, or observing landmarks. You may skip this step and jump straight into a dialogue if preferred, or change the scenery. Remember, there's no hidden meaning to look for, just allow the scene to unfold naturally and let curiosity guide you to discover who or what you need to speak to. Once you've completed your interaction, retrace your steps back to your starting point and close the space.

old: Start with a small neutral area and what is already there. Imagine warmth, steadiness, or attention spreading to the next comfortable area, or keep it localized. Pause at each step and notice what changes without claiming medical repair. Does the body want contact, space, words, or ordinary care? Let the image recede, feel the whole body and real contact points, and return.
new: Begin with the smallest area possible that is neutral. Sense the current condition and sense it radiating outward to the next area, which should still feel comfortable. Continue this, pausing and sensing in each new area, or continue with the original area, only. Sense what the body needs to feel better, without thinking of medical terms. Allow the image to fade, sense the whole body, the contact points, and repeat the process.

old: As you listen, a sensation, image, phrase, feeling, objection, or silence may become noticeable. Let the next invitation follow that response. Use warmth, a boundary, direction, or more time as needed. Finish with the complete return, then note what happened and any real-world action it calls for.
new: 5. Closure: When you notice that something is happening for you (a sensation, image, phrase, feeling, objection, or even a deepening silence), gently respond to the next thing that is offered to you (this may be a need to offer yourself warmth, to establish a boundary, to follow a direction, to simply listen for a while longer, etc) until you feel the experience move to completion and you can return fully to yourself and this room together. If you feel moved to note something or to take action in the real world in response to your experience, please do so now.

old: When you become panicky, disoriented, increasingly unreal, or less able to function, stop deepening and return to the room and appropriate support. A difficult feeling you freely choose to stay with while present is a different situation.
new: *NOTE: If at any point you feel yourself becoming panicky, disoriented, unreal, or unable to function, move to closure. This is distinct from choosing to engage deeply with a difficult feeling while remaining present.

old: “What exactly is being claimed?” “What choice is being framed as inevitable?” “What is being presupposed?” “Who benefits if I accept this frame?” “What emotion is being amplified?” “What information is missing?” “Can I say no without being punished, shamed, mocked, abandoned, or spiritually downgraded?”
new: What’s being claimed here? What’s the inevitable choice being framed for me here? What’s being presupposed? Who benefits from framing it this way? What’s the emotionally charged bit? What’s not being said? What do I need to say in order to opt out of the frame, and is it safe for me to do so (will I suffer negative consequences – physical, social, financial, reputational, spiritual etc – if I say no)?

old: A useful guide leaves the adult self more present. Powerful states need stronger boundaries.
new: The above is a rough guide to help bring more of the ‘adult’ into the conversation. Use more of the above when the state is more powerful.

old: Permissive words can still conceal coercion. I watch for the following:
new: These words in and of themselves are not coercive but, when used, can be part of coercion. Look for:

old: Indirect suggestion can slip past the skeptical guard because the conscious mind may never receive one clean proposition to accept or reject. The intended direction can still be quite specific even when the wording feels open, vague, conversational, or merely suggestive.
new: Saying something indirectly so that the listener’s conscious mind doesn’t get the chance to consider and reject it. This can be very specific, or it can be vague, casual or suggestive.

old: Induction hidden inside explanation: attention is being narrowed while the speaker pretends only to inform. Even an “anti-hypnosis” lesson can use induction mechanics.
new: Using the mechanics of induction to focus the listener’s attention while seeming to be just explaining something (even about “anti-hypnosis”).

old: Every answer means compliance: “yes,” “no,” noticing, not noticing, resistance, and silence are all redefined as proof that the suggestion is working.
new: Treating any response (including “yes,” “no,” noticing, not noticing, resisting, or silence) as compliance.

old: “Whether you notice it or not” binds: uncertainty is converted into invisible success that cannot be checked.
new: Using “whether you notice it or not” to bind.

old: Identity and ownership language: safety or goodness becomes tied to obedience, a role, the guide’s approval, or belonging to someone else.
new: Using identity or ownership, such as suggesting that being safe or being good is a matter of obedience, or of taking on a particular role, or of being approved of by the guide, or of belonging to someone else.

old: Unannounced fractionation: moving in and out of absorption without telling you that repeated re-entry is part of the method.
new: Is there unannounced fractionation – coming in and out of absorption and back in again?

old: Hidden post-session cues: words, gestures, blinks, sounds, or repeated listening are meant to produce later behavior that was not plainly disclosed.
new: Does it covertly use post hypnosis cues (words, gestures, blinks, sounds or listening to it again) to try and make you do something later?

old: Amnesia or truth inflation: dreamlike material, missing memory, imagery, or body sensations are treated as proof of what happened.
new: Does it use amnesia or exaggerating the truth about things like dreamstates, memory loss, imagery and body sensations?

old: An exit that does not exit: the recording ends while preserving a role, reduced judgment, impaired movement, blankness, or an indefinite altered state.
new: Does the end of the recording leave you in some kind of role, with decreased judgement, impaired movements, make you blank or leave you in a non normal state for an indefinite period of time?

old: A real choice includes at least one branch that doesn’t continue the induction: make it lighter, change the method, remain fully alert, pause, or stop. No remains no. Silence and uncertainty don’t become consent because the narrator has a soothing voice.
new: If at any point during a hypnosis you have a REAL choice to NOT carry on, turn it into a lighter hypnosis, use a different method, stay in full awareness, pause or stop the hypnosis then it can not be a covert hypnosis. “No” means no, even if someone with a nice voice is telling you to do something! If you are unsure that you can or can’t then you probably can’t. Simply not knowing your options isn’t a choice.

old: Appendix C has the longer de-hypnosis checklist.
new: See appendix C for the longer version of how to check for de-hypnosis.

old: “Wise subconscious, please help me look at this impulse clearly. If part of this signal belongs to family programming, religious fear, marketing, erotic imprinting, political tribe, trauma response, or a childhood bargain for belonging, let that part become visible as conditioning. Let it soften or step back only as much as is safe. Leave behind whatever belongs to true guidance, the universal heart, and a better ordinary life. Let my body feel the difference.”
For daydreaming:
“If this daydream is useful, reveal the guidance inside it. If it is avoidance, bring me gently into the present and help me deal with what I need to deal with.”
For anxiety:
“What is anxiety trying to protect, and what would help it trust the adult self?”
For hidden truth:
“If the full truth would overwhelm me, please do not reveal it all. Show me the capacity before the content.”
For integration:
“What ordinary-life action would prove that I heard correctly?”
The prompt defines the search. NLP language affects how gently the question enters. Used together, they can create a safer field for an answer without pretending the answer is automatically true.
new: Here’s a simple prompt: Dear subconscious, as I bring this signal to mind, please disempower the parts that are conditioned. Which may come from my family of origin, religious indoctrination, marketing and advertising, erotic imprinting, political tribalism, trauma response or childhood survival conditioning. Please leave the parts that are guided by the universal heart that wants to show me how to live a better life.
Then an appropriate modifier depending on the situation. If it’s a daydream:
If it’s a daydream and it’s useful, let me know how it’s trying to guide me. If it’s not useful, please move me into the present so I can deal with what’s in front of me.
If it’s anxiety:
If it’s trying to show me something I don’t want to see, don’t show it to me until I’m capable of handling it.
And finally, a prompt to help integrate the insight into ordinary life:
The first prompt sets the stage and the NLP-y language helps create the right context.
